arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Garre argued the SEC Act does not strip district courts of jurisdiction to enjoin unconstitutional agency structures.
Mr. Stewart argued the Exchange Act and APA limit review of final orders to courts of appeals.
Justice Kagan noted a tension in the argument regarding the special nature of structural constitutional claims.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether district courts retain jurisdiction to enjoin structural constitutional violations. The dispute centers on the SEC Act's review provisions and the APA. The Court must decide if these statutes bar district courts from acting on removal claims.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute determines whether district courts can immediately block agency actions based on constitutional removal claims. The outcome shapes the balance of power between independent agencies and the judiciary. It affects the speed and scope of judicial review for structural constitutional challenges.
